slides.say: A game machine shows a three-digit number. Its hundreds digit is six, its tens digit is one, and its units digit is X. The machine pays four tokens if the number is divisible by two but not by three, eight tokens if it is divisible by three but not by two, and twelve tokens if it is divisible by both two and three. Noa played once and won twelve tokens. How many different values can X have?

A long story, but the only thing that matters is the twelve tokens. Twelve tokens means the number divides by two and by three. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, with three first, and then with two first.
at: divides by two and by three

slides.say: [short pause] Let's start with three. The digit sum must divide by three. Six plus one is seven, so the sum is seven plus X.
X is one digit, zero to nine, so seven plus X is between seven and sixteen. The multiples of three in there are nine, twelve and fifteen. So X is two, five or eight.
Now two. Six one two ends in two, even. Six one five ends in five, odd, so it's out. Six one eight ends in eight, even. So X has two values, two and eight, and choice number two is our answer.
at: choice number two is our answer

slides.say: Now careful, three is the trap. Those are the three digits that work for three, but five makes an odd number.
[pause] Another way is to start with two. The number must be even, so X is zero, two, four, six or eight.

Now the digit sums. Seven plus zero is seven, seven plus two is nine, seven plus four is eleven, seven plus six is thirteen, and seven plus eight is fifteen. Only nine and fifteen divide by three, so X is two or eight. Two values, choice number two. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
